channel.title: Israel National News Flashes
channel.description: Latest news flashes from Israel National News

item.title: 17-year-old girl moderately injured in motorcycle accident in Modi’in
item.description:
A 17-year-old girl was moderately injured after the motorcycle she was riding was struck by a vehicle in Modi’in.
Magen David Adom paramedics evacuated her to Shamir-Assaf Harofeh Hospital.

item.title: Syrian President: It is not possible for October 7 to dictate Israel’s policies
item.description: Speaking in New York, Syrian President Ahmad al-Sharaa says Israel withdrew from security talks after the sides had nearly reached an agreement, while insisting the Golan Heights are Syrian.

item.title: Report: IDF carries out controlled explosion in southern Lebanon
item.description: Lebanese media reported that the IDF carried out a large controlled explosion near the town of Khiam in southern Lebanon.

item.description: Iranian media reported that explosions were heard coming from the sea near Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz.

item.title: Gadi Eisenkot criticizes Macron: The statement is radically detached from reality
item.description:
Yashar chairman Gadi Eisenkot criticized remarks by French President Emmanuel Macron, emphasizing that the Hamas terrorist organization also operates in Judea and Samaria and poses a threat to Israeli civilians.
“French President Macron’s statement is radically detached from the reality on the ground. As someone who commanded the Judea and Samaria Division and fought to eradicate Hamas terrorism, I know very well about the terrorist organization’s activities in Judea and Samaria and the threat it poses to Israeli civilians, as we witnessed just two days ago in the deadly attack in Binyamin."

item.title: Two suspects arrested following pursuit near Jordanian border
item.description:
IDF surveillance soldiers on Tuesday evening detected suspicious movement along the Jordanian border in the Jordan Valley area. IDF, Border Police forces in Judea and Samaria, and the Israel Police Judea and Samaria District launched a pursuit.
According to the IDF, two suspects were apprehended shortly afterward and transferred to security forces for further questioning.

item.title: PM's office: The absurd statement by Emmanuel Macron is astounding
item.description:
Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's office on Tuesday evening blasted French President Emmanuel Macron who claimed at the UN that Hamas "has never been very active in Judea and Samaria".
“The grotesque absurdity of Emmanuel Macron's statement is staggering. On Sunday, the eve of Yom Kippur, just two days ago, Netanel Shakron - a FRENCH CITIZEN and father of six - was murdered in his car by a Hamas terrorist in Judea and Samaria. With his final breath, he told his son to run," the statement said. “Hamas terrorists carry out attacks against Jews almost every day. They have murdered countless Israeli civilians in Judea and Samaria. Ignorance is NO EXCUSE for erasing their blood."

item.title: Soldiers of the Great Liberation: In Memory of Enid-Esther and Stuart Wortsman
item.description: The Wortsmans refused to rest, maintaining the struggle to free Soviet Jewry through dark and difficult years until the regime finally collapsed, resulting in the historic exodus of over a million Soviet Jews to Israel. In memoriam.

item.title: Prof. Anne Bayefsky blasts Guterres UN speech: 'This blood libel is patently false'
item.description: Human rights scholar Anne Bayefsky sharply condemns UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres following his General Assembly speech: ‘The United Nations is a very dangerous organization with enormous power.’

item.title: ‘Earthquake in the prisons’: The message from Sinwar that was misinterpreted in Israel
item.description: Weeks before October 7, a message was received from Sinwar about an “earthquake in the prisons." Israel’s security establishment assessed that it was connected to Tsurkov.

item.title: Macron at UN: Hamas has never been very active in Judea and Samaria
item.description: The French President criticized developments in Judea and Samaria and told the UN General Assembly: “Hamas has never been very active in the West Bank."

item.title: French Pres. claims Hamas has been very active in Judea and Samaria
item.description: French President Emmanuel Macron referred to what is happening in Judea and Samaria and said: "Just look at what is happening in the West Bank. Day after day, we witness violations. And in the name of what? Hamas has never been particularly active in the West Bank."

item.title: PM to Shakron family: 'Terrorist who murdered Netanel might be the first to be executed'
item.description: Netanyahu tells slain victim’s son: 'His case could be the first to invoke the death penalty law for terrorists.'

item.title: Yosef Haddad receives graphic death threats
item.description:
Yosef Haddad, an advocacy activist and candidate number 2 on the "Amach Yisrael" list, received a series of e-mails this evening containing explicit threats to his life, including: "We will cut off your fingers one by one and dismember your body along with the Americans."
According to the party's statement, it is believed that the threats were sent by elements linked to the Iranian regime.

item.title: Smotrich slams Guterres: 'He endangers the lives of half a million Jews'
item.description: Smotrich sharply criticized the UN Secretary-General following his speech at the General Assembly: “The UN Secretary-General’s wild incitement gives a tailwind to terrorism."

item.title: ShinyHunters claims major FBI hack, thousands of employees’ data stolen
item.description: Hackers claim to have stolen highly sensitive personal data on thousands of FBI employees, including home addresses, phone numbers and information about their spouses, after allegedly breaching bureau systems.

item.title: Hackers claim to have hacked FBI, obtained info on thousands of employees
item.description: The hacker group "ShinyHunters" claims to have managed to hack into the US Federal Bureau of Investigation's systems and obtain information regarding thousands of the FBI's employees.

item.title: Activists cross the border into Syria, cause IDF to respond
item.description: 14 Israelis crossed the border into Syria, calling for settlement in the area. An IDF force was dispatched, located them, and returned them to Israel. The military is demanding that legal action be taken against them.

item.title: Ontario: Yom Kippur shooter dies of his wounds
item.description:
Sean Ward, the suspect who carried out the shooting attack near the Sons of Jacob synagogue in the town of Belleville, Ontario, died of his wounds in the hospital.
Ward was critically injured in an exchange of gunfire with Officer Jeff Smith on Yom Kippur Eve. The officer was seriously injured and is in stable condition.

item.title: Danon praises Trump’s UN address: Together, we will continue to confront the axis of evil
item.description: Israel’s UN Ambassador Danny Danon praised US President Donald Trump for his address to the UN General Assembly, highlighting the US-Israel alliance, the Abraham Accords and efforts to expand the circle of peace.

item.title: UK: 2 arrested for plot to atack Manchester Jewish community
item.description: British security forces announced that they had arrested two suspects on suspicion of planning to carry out a terrorist attack against the Jewish community in Manchester.

item.title: Between Iran & Oman: Haredi reporter sails into heart of tensions in Strait of Hormuz
item.description: Haredi journalist Yitzhak Horowitz reached Oman’s Musandam Peninsula - one of the world’s most strategic and tense locations - and shared his impressions from the area.

item.title: 14 Israeli civilians cross Syrian border
item.description:
A short while ago, 14 Israeli civilians arrived in the Alonei Habashan area and crossed the border into Syria. IDF soldiers were dispatched to the area and operated to locate them and returned the civilians to Israeli territory.
The detained civilians were transferred to the Israel Police for further handling.

item.title: Huckabee: No path to peace until 'pay for slay' ends
item.description:
US Ambassador to Israel reiterated America's demand that the Palestinian Authority end its 'pay for slay' policy following Sunday's deadly shooting attack in Binyamin.
"The US has long demanded that the PA end 'pay for slay' that rewards terrorists for murdering Jews. There will be no peace or a path forward until payment for murder ends," Huckabee stated.

item.title: Palestinian refugees in Tel Aviv
item.description: Expelled from their homes and forced to live in huts and tents near the sea, the Palestinian refugees had no one to defend them - at first. Op-ed.

item.title: 'Dad, can you hear me?': Yoav recalls his final moments with his father
item.description: Yoav Shakron, son of Netanel Shakron, recalls his final conversation and pre-Yom Kippur immersion with his father: 'He always smiled and made sure others smiled too.'
